items.prompt: Tap every square you think the white rook on d4 can move to. A wrong guess costs nothing; you will see why afterwards. (The kings only fill the position.)

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the rook on d4 can move to.

hints: A rook goes along rows and columns. Which row and column cross at d4?
Rows are ranks and columns are files. Which squares share the d-file or the fourth rank with the rook?
Nothing stands in the way, so every square on the d-file and on the fourth rank counts, fourteen in all.
items.explain: The rook reaches every square on its file and on its rank: seven up and down the d-file, seven along the fourth rank. Nothing blocks it, so the count is fourteen.

items.prompt: Move the white rook (the tower-shaped piece) to the top row of the board (the eighth rank) in one move.

claims.statement: The rook can go from b3 to b8.

hints: The eighth rank is the top row, where Black's pieces start.
Which line goes straight up from b3?
The b-file: b4, b5, b6, b7, b8. Is it clear?
items.explain: The rook slides straight up the b-file from b3 to b8, five squares, because nothing stands on the way.

feedback_by_move.b3h3: That keeps the rook on the third rank. It does not reach the top edge.
feedback_by_move.b3a3: That moves the rook sideways, along the third rank, and not to the top row.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white rook on e4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the rook on e4 can move to.

hints: Take one direction at a time: up, down, left, right.
Your own pawns stop the rook before their squares. Enemy pawns can be taken, and the line ends there.
Up: e5 only. Down: e3 only. Left: d4, c4 and the capture on b4. Right: f4 and the capture on g4.
items.explain: Up the file the white pawn on e6 stops the rook after e5, and down the file the white pawn on e2 stops it after e3. Left and right, the black pawns on b4 and g4 can be captured, and the lines end there.

items.prompt: Two black pawns stand on h5 and h6 above the white rook on h2. Can the rook reach h6 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: h6 is behind the pawn on h5.
The rook can capture on h5.

hints: Which piece does the rook meet first on the h-file?
Which squares lie between the rook and h6?
What does the rook do when it reaches an enemy piece?
items.explain: The rook meets the pawn on h5 first. It can capture that pawn, but a rook cannot jump, so h6 stays out of reach this move.

items.prompt: The white rook on c2 wants to capture the black pawn on f5, but cannot do so in one move. Find a move after which the rook could capture it next turn.

claims.statement: f5 is not on the c-file or the second rank.
After the rook goes to f2 it attacks f5.
After the rook goes to c5 it attacks f5.

hints: Which squares share a line with f5?
The f-file and the fifth rank both pass through f5.
Can the rook reach the f-file or the fifth rank in one move?
items.explain: f5 lies on the f-file and the fifth rank. The rook can reach f2 (same file as f5) or c5 (same rank as f5) in one move, and from either square the pawn is one slide away.

feedback_by_move.c2c4: c4 is on neither the f-file nor the fifth rank, so the rook still cannot reach f5.
feedback_by_move.c2h2: h2 is not on the f-file or the fifth rank, so the pawn on f5 is still out of reach.

items.prompt: Capture a black pawn with the white rook.

claims.statement: The rook can capture on e5.
d6 is neither on the a-file nor on the fifth rank.

hints: Which pawn stands on a line with the rook?
Is the other pawn on the rook's rank or file?
Check the squares between a5 and the pawn.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 is on the rook's rank and the squares between are empty. The pawn on d6 is not on the rook's lines, so the rook cannot take it.

feedback_by_move.a5d6: d6 is not on the rook's rank or file, so a rook cannot go there.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white rook can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the rook on d5 can move to.

hints: Trace each of the four directions to its end.
Which pieces are yours, which are the enemy's?
A line ends before your own piece and on an enemy piece.
items.explain: The rook is stopped by its own pawns on d6 and f5, so it cannot go up and can go right only as far as e5. Down, it takes the pawn on d3. Left, it takes the pawn on a5. That makes 6 squares: a5, b5, c5, d3, d4, e5.

items.prompt: How many squares can the white rook reach in one move?

claims.statement: The rook on b2 has two legal moves.

hints: Check each direction in turn.
Check each of the four directions: which are open?
Look for the squares left (a2) and below (b1).
items.explain: The pawns on b3 and c2 block two directions at once. The rook can still go to a2, to the left, and to b1, below. Two squares.

items.prompt: A black pawn stands on g6 and the white rook on g2. Can the rook reach g6 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook can capture on g6: g3, g4 and g5 are empty.

hints: Which squares lie between g2 and g6?
What happens when the rook arrives on an enemy piece?
items.explain: g3, g4 and g5 are empty, and the pawn on g6 is an enemy piece, so the rook takes it and stops there.

items.prompt: A black pawn stands on f5 and the white rook on b5. Can the rook reach h5 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: h5 is behind the pawn on f5.
The rook can capture on f5.

hints: Which squares lie between the rook and h5?
What can the rook do with the first enemy piece it meets, and what then?
items.explain: The pawn on f5 ends the slide. The rook may take it, but g5 and h5 behind it are out of reach this move.

items.prompt: The white rook is on h3, its own pawn on h5, and a black pawn on c3. Can the rook reach c3 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook can capture on c3: g3, f3, e3 and d3 are empty.
h6 is behind the white pawn on h5.

hints: Which line leads from h3 to c3?
Which squares lie between the rook and c3, and who stands on them?
items.explain: The squares between h3 and c3 are empty. The pawn on c3 is an enemy piece, so the rook takes it. The pawn on h5 is the rook's own and matters only to the file.

items.prompt: Capture one of the black knights with the white rook.

claims.statement: The rook can capture on e7.
c4 is neither on the e-file nor on the third rank.

hints: Which knight stands on the rook's file or rank?
Which squares lie between the rook and that knight?
items.explain: The knight on e7 is on the e-file with e4, e5 and e6 empty. The knight on c4 is off the rook's lines.

feedback_by_move.e3c4: c4 is not on the rook's rank or file, so the rook cannot go there.

items.prompt: A black pawn stands on g4, one step diagonally up and right from the white rook on f3. Can the rook take it in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook cannot capture on g4.
The rook can move straight up one square.

hints: Is g4 on the rook's column or on its row?
The rook is on the f-file and the third rank. Which file and rank is g4 on?
A rook only captures along a row or a column, never diagonally.
items.explain: The pawn is on g4, which is on neither the f-file nor the third rank. A rook never moves or captures diagonally, so it cannot take the pawn from f3.

items.prompt: Can the white rook go from c3 to e5 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: e5 is off the rook's file and rank.

hints: Which file and which rank is the rook on?
Is e5 on the c-file? Is it on rank 3?
e5 is on neither, so reaching it would need a diagonal.
items.explain: The rook is on the c-file and rank 3. The square e5 is on the e-file and rank 5, so it shares neither line with the rook. A rook never moves diagonally, so it cannot get there in one move.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white rook can move to. It may stop on any square along the way, and taking is allowed but never forced.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the rook on d4 can move to.

hints: Follow the rook along its row and its column, one direction at a time.
Your own pawn stops the rook on the square before it. The black pawn can be taken, and that ends the slide.
Count four squares to the right, one to the left, three down and two up.
items.explain: To the left the rook stops before its own pawn. Upward it may stop on the empty square or take the black pawn, but it cannot go past. Right and down are open to the edge.
